paragraphs.dominant_move: state the energy-design object and bind the simplifications to the baseline
compress force analysis, governing equations and the analytical energy output
contrast the circle and ellipse branches through their analytical and numerical methods
escalate the planar curve-family study to the downhill three-dimensional case
preview a common sensitivity coefficient and comparative factor reading
move from the theoretical optimum through practical tradeoffs to the selected design
establish the halfpipe setting and motivate shape as a performance-and-safety decision
translate the prompt into three ordered design tasks
use the energy balance to motivate the circle-to-ellipse two-dimensional model ladder
complete the roadmap with the three-dimensional extension and practical criteria

global_organization_chain: Open with the complete energy-to-design storyline and headline outputs.
Translate the prompt into three linked design tasks under one energy-balance lens.
Stabilize symbols, geometry and simplifying assumptions before deriving equations.
Derive a general profile-dependent dissipative energy model.
Reduce the functional problem first to an analytical circle and then to a numerical ellipse.
Add collision and air loss in stages so each component changes an observable design surface.
Report factor responses and local sensitivity only after the design branches are established.
Reuse the two-dimensional model through an explicit coordinate transform for the downhill case.
Convert the theoretical slope criterion into safety, construction and athletic-performance tradeoffs.
Close in body order, preserving the distinction between theoretical and practically adjusted outputs.

main_argument_chains.claim: A general dissipative energy relation can organize the halfpipe shape study before choosing a particular curve family.
support_steps: Define geometry, normal force, frictional loss and mechanical energy.
Derive the profile-dependent energy ODE and collision initial condition.
Express final energy as a functional of the course profile.
Restrict that functional first to a circle and then to an ellipse.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The paper obtains an analytical baseline and a more flexible numerical design branch from one shared physical object.

main_argument_chains.claim: Collision loss materially changes the ellipse design surface and therefore cannot be omitted from the design model.
support_steps: Remove collision while retaining snow friction.
Observe a degenerate right-angle limit as either ellipse axis approaches zero.
Restore collision and observe an interior peak in the semi-major axis.
Select the semi-major axis by peak comparison while recognizing the semi-minor axis remains boundary-selected.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The negative ablation justifies the collision component and changes how the reported ellipse optimum must be interpreted.

main_argument_chains.claim: Local factor importance is made comparable only after a common response definition and baseline design are fixed.
support_steps: Fix the ellipse design point and hold the boundary semi-minor axis convention.
Define a normalized local sensitivity coefficient.
Vary six named inputs one at a time.
Report the complete coefficient vector before interpreting importance.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The reader can compare local directions while retaining the boundary that this is not joint or structural robustness.

main_argument_chains.claim: The planar design is extended to a downhill course by reusing the existing energy model after a coordinate transformation.
support_steps: Introduce downhill distance and slope geometry.
Map a sloped section to transformed two-dimensional coordinates.
Recompute the ellipse response under slope changes.
Use equal hanging heights and spline interpolation to select a theoretical slope.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The model yields a traceable three-dimensional design stage before practical adjustments are introduced.

main_argument_chains.claim: The energy-based theoretical design is intentionally not the final practical recommendation.
support_steps: Identify safety tradeoffs in edge and slope angles.
Retain a bottom segment for rider preparation despite friction loss.
Add snow-retention constructability and twist requirements.
Adjust the theoretical slope while preserving its provenance in the conclusion.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The final values are presented as a practical adjustment to a theoretical result, not as the output of one unchanged objective.

warnings.warning: The printed post-collision speed is dimensionally invalid: it places mass inside the square root and gravity in the denominator. The following energy equation is consistent with the intended mass-independent relation, so future work must reconcile adjacent equations with a unit check.

The rendered sensitivity definition uses the inverse normalization factor A/B, whereas a dimensionless elasticity requires B/A; the reported coefficients appear to follow the intended form. Future work must reconcile the printed definition with the calculation before interpreting sensitivities.

The coordinate transform mixes an along-slope distance with unresolved horizontal and vertical projections. Future dimensional extensions must define the distance convention first and resolve both components consistently before reusing the two-dimensional energy model.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Aligned small multiples reveal circle-radius response and boundary behavior with fixed inputs shown in-panel.
Paired final-energy curves distinguish an interior semi-major-axis peak from monotone boundary behavior in the semi-minor axis.
Six compact sensitivity curves expose response sign, nonlinearity and relative local influence.
The three-dimensional sketch and repeated response-curve grammar connect geometry to the reused two-dimensional model.
The slope-response figures carry the final theoretical decision while their copied captions provide a reusable warning about figure-to-claim traceability.
